newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa metal workers reject employers' pay offer.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa metal workers reject employers' pay offer.

text.p: Metal and engineering workers rejected the employers' wage offer in the first round of official talks, employers said on Thursday.

The Steel and Engineering Industries Federation of South Africa (SEIFSA) said in a statement the workers were demanding more than the offer and another round of wage talks would take place on May 20 and 21.
"Representatives of the industry's nine trade unions, whose wage demands range from 18 to 21.4 percent, rejected the employer offer and argued for...a greater wage increase," SEIFSA said.
Employers made an offer to increase both scheduled and actual wage rates by six percent, raising the industry's minimum wage by 44 cents an hour to 7.84 rand or around 1,483 rand a month.
Unions also put forward 63 non-wage demands, the majority of which were rejected by employers, SEIFSA said.

These included a reduction in work hours to 40 per week without loss of pay, an increase in annual leave, an increase in shift work allowances and overtime rates, the introduction of 200 hours of training per worker annually and the extension of maternity leave to non-scheduled workers.
Employers non-wage proposals included raising subsistence allowances by six percent and reducing the minimum number of qualifying shifts for purposes of pro rata leave pay and bonus.
They also offered to improve maternity leave benefits and introduce maternity leave for adoptive mothers.
Around 9,000 companies employing about 285,000 hourly paid workers operate in the industry.

Trade unions parties include the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa and the Chemical Workers Industrial Union which are affiliated to the Congress of South African Trade Unions, the country's largest union federation.
